caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3346 of 2014
lawyer:
For the Petitioner Ms. Hosneara Begum, Advocate, instructed by Modhumalati, Advocate-on- Record. 
For Respondent No. 1: Mr. S. N. Goswami, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record.
parties:
Sonali Bank Limited ----- Petitioner
Versus
Md. Humayun Kabir and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Ms. Nazmun Ara Sultana, J: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, at the instance of the Sonali Bank Limited, is directed against the Judgment and order dated 20.05.2014 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Rule No. 880(FM)(Con) of 2011 arising out of First Miscellaneous Appeal Tender No.632 of 2011 making the rule absolute. 

 This leave-petitioner-Sonali Bank Limited instituted Artha Rin Suit No.623 of 2004 in Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka against the respondent Nos.2 to 5 herein for realization of outstanding dues of Tk.70,70,436.28/- as on 31.03.2004. The said suit was decreed ex-pane by the judgment and decree dated 08.09.2004. The decree-holder bank thereafter filed Artha Execution Case No.I89 of 2005 on the basis of the said decree. During pendency of that execution case the respondent No. I herein, namely, Md. Humayun Kabir filed an application on 12.10.2005 in that Artha Execution Case No.189 of 2005 under Order I Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for being added as a party in that execution case which was summarily rejected on 17.10.2005. 

 3. Being aggrieved by that order the respondent No. I herein filed Writ Petition No.8021 of 2005 which was dismissed on 19.06.2008. The respondent No. I herein then filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1329 of 2008 challenging that order of dismissal dated 19.06.2008, but ultimately that Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal also was dismissed as not pressed. The respondent No. I herein again filed an application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 27.04.2009 in that Artha Execution Case No.1 89 of 2005 claiming some of the mortgage properties to be his own. The said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No.25 of 2009. The Artha Rin Adalat, after hearing, rejected that miscellaneous case by order No.49 dated 15.06.2009 for non deposit of - the requisite security of 10% of the decreetal dues as required under Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 29.07.2009, the respondent No.1 herein filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1700 of 2009 before this Division. This Division, aft& hearing, dismissed that Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal by the judgment and order dated 25.08.2011 holding to the effect that the Artha Rin Adalat rightly rejected the application of the leave-petitioner under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for not depositing the security as per Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and that the order of the Aruba Rin Adalat rejecting the application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure was passed in accordance with Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003. The respondent No. I herein thereafter filed First Miscellaneous Appeal being FMAT No.632 of 2011 against the same order No.49 dated 15.06.2009 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat rejecting the application under Order XXI 4 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a prayer for condonation of delay of 814 days and a rule was issued on the said prayer being Civil Rule No.880(FM) (Con) of 2011. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing. condoned the delay of 814 days and made the rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 20.05.2004. In making the rule absolute the learned Judges of the High Court Division made some observations to the effect that just one day before pronouncement of the ex-parte judgment in the Artha Rin Suit in question the schedule to the plaint and also the mortgage, deed were amended by inserting C.S. Plot No.I55 in place of C.S. Plot No.150 which was initially mentioned in the schedule to the plaint and also in the mortgage deed, without giving any notice to the petitioner who was the holder of that Plot No.155 and that this fact proves that fraud was practiced in obtaining the ex-parte judgment and decree. The High Court Division thus held also that in such facts and circumstances appellant shall not be - required to pay 10% decreetal amount. The High Court Division held thus : 

 6. Ms. Hosneara Begum, the learned Advocate appearing for the leave-petitioner Sonali Bank has made submission to the effect that admittedly mortgagor Monowara Islam acquired this mortgage property by a registered deed dated 03.04.1990 from the government and in that registered deed this land was described mentioning its municipality holding number and four boundaries and the C.S. Plot number was not mentioned, but at the time of creation of the mortgage deed, the learned Advocate mistakenly mentioned a wrong C.S. plot and consequently in the schedule to the plaint also this wrong C.S. plot number was mentioned, but subsequently this mistake was duly corrected as per provision of law; that save and except the plot number only all other identifying features, i.e. the holding number and boundaries were correctly mentioned in both the mortgage deed and in the schedule to the plaint which were not changed at all by the subsequent amendment. The learned Advocate has argued that in these circumstances the subsequent amendment made in the plaint and also in the mortgage deed by inserting the correct plot number only in place of the incorrect plot number does not tell at all of any fraud. The learned Advocate has argued also that this petitioner-respondent Md. Humayun Kabir was very much aware of the filing of the Artha Rin Suit, the passing of the decree therein, the filing of the execution case, but inspite of that he did not take any step as per Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 on depositing the requisite security and instead he filed an application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure without making any deposit as per Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as such the said application was rightly rejected upto the Appellate Division and thereafter the respondent No.1 filed FMAT No.632 of 2011 against the same order No.49 dated 15.06.2009 rejecting the application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure after a long delay of 814 days. The learned Advocate has argued that the High Court Division has committed great injustice in condoning the delay of long 814 days in the above stated facts and circumstances of the case. The learned Advocate has contended also that the High Court Division committed illegality also in making observations to the effect that fraud was practiced in obtaining the ex-parte decree in Artha Rin Suit in disposing of an application for condonation of delay. The learned Advocate has argued that in this case no fraud was practiced at all by inserting the correct plot number in place of a wrong plot number which was mentioned in the schedule to the plaint and also in the mortgage deed through mistake specially where the municipality holding number and also the four boundaries of this and as were mentioned in the schedule to the plaint and m the mortgage deed remained unaltered. The learned Advocate has argued to the effect also that in fact this is an ill device to prolong the execution case and thereby to delay the realization of the decreetal amount.
